title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Tate's work on p-divisible groups (letter to Tate, May 1966; Tate's Driebergen paper 1966/67). Let K be a complete discretely valued field of mixed characteristic (0,p), π = Gal(K̄/K), C the completion of K̄. Let G be a p-divisible group over O_K with Tate module M = T_p(G), a free Z_p-module of finite type, and V = M ⊗_{Z_p} C. Grothendieck lists three structures on V.
(1) A Hodge–Tate decomposition V = V^{10} ⊕ V^{01} of C-vector spaces. A crossed-out version writes V^{10} = V̌^0 ⊗ C and V^{01} = V̌^1 ⊗_K C(1).
(2) A semilinear action of π on V, compatible with the action of π on C.
(3) The integral structure V ≅ M ⊗_{Z_p} C, with M free of finite type over Z_p ('réseau' corrected to 'module libre de t.f.').
He then records how the structures relate.
- (1)+(2): V^{10} = V^π ⊗_K C and V^{01} = (V ⊗ C(1))^π ⊗_K C(-1). This is Tate's theorem combined with C(i)^π = 0 for i ≠ 0 (Tate–Sen). Hence the margin note '2 ⇒ 1': the Galois action determines the decomposition.
- (2)+(3): M is stable under π. Structures 2 and 3 (hence 1, 2, 3) amount to a Z_p-lattice M with continuous π-action. By Tate's full faithfulness this essentially recovers the p-divisible group over K.
- (3)+(1): marked '???'. This is the open question of how the lattice and the Hodge–Tate data relate.
NB: the field K enters only through (2). Structures (1) and (3) look intrinsic to p-divisible groups over Ŝ = Ω̂ = C, i.e. over O_C, with no Galois action. This is effectively a Riemann-type question: is a p-divisible group over O_C described by its Tate lattice plus Hodge–Tate data, as a complex torus is described by a lattice plus a complex structure?
Finally he defines the smallest algebraic subgroup G ⊂ GL(M ⊗ Q_p) (written Q_ℓ) such that G_C contains the operators diag(λ, ξ) acting by λ on V^{10} and by ξ on V^{01}. In modern terms this is the image of the Hodge–Tate cocharacter (plus scalars), and G is the p-adic analogue of the Mumford–Tate group: Serre's 'Hodge–Tate group'. Its purpose is presumably to bound or describe the image of π, in the spirit of Serre and Sen.
errors: Over O_C without Galois action, the intrinsic Hodge–Tate datum is only a filtration (the Hodge–Tate exact sequence 0 → Lie(G)⊗C(1) → T⊗C → ω_{G^∨}⊗C → 0), not a canonical splitting. The decomposition V^{10} ⊕ V^{01} needs the Galois action (2). So the NB claim that (1) is intrinsic over C is inaccurate as stated; only the subspace (the filtration) is intrinsic.
'2 ⇒ 1' holds only for Hodge–Tate representations, which is automatic for those coming from p-divisible groups.
The 'Q_ℓ' in M⊗Q_ℓ should be Q_p, since M is a Z_p-module.
The notation C[1] presumably denotes the Tate twist C(1).

ideas.what: Hodge–Tate decomposition of T_p(G)⊗C, recovered from the Galois action via invariants of Tate twists
ideas.where_published: Letter to Tate May 1966 (unpublished); Tate's Driebergen paper

ideas.what: Structures 2+3 equal a Galois-stable Z_p-lattice, i.e. p-divisible groups over K via Tate's full faithfulness
Observation that the Tate lattice and the Hodge–Tate data are intrinsic over O_C, independent of K, with the question of their relation
ideas.modern_name: Classification of p-divisible groups over O_C by (T, W ⊂ T⊗C(-1))

ideas.what: Smallest algebraic group over Q_p whose C-points contain the Hodge–Tate operators diag(λ, ξ)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre ('Groupes algébriques associés aux modules de Hodge-Tate', Astérisque 65, 1979); Sen 1973 (Lie algebra of the Galois image)

missed.claim: Grothendieck isolates the pair (Tate lattice, Hodge–Tate data) as intrinsic to p-divisible groups over Ĉ (O_C), independent of K and Galois. He asks ('3 et 1 ???') for their relation. This is a Riemann-style classification problem that was solved only much later by Scholze–Weinstein.
missed.quote: NB le corps K intervient dans 2) ... mais pas dans 1), ni 3), qui semblent des structures intrinsèques à la donnée des groupes p-divisibles sur Ŝ = Ω̂ = C
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This shows that the idea of studying p-divisible groups over O_C via linear-algebra data (lattice plus Hodge–Tate filtration) was in Grothendieck's mind, if the dating is early. That is a historical precursor to Fargues and Scholze–Weinstein.

missed.claim: Grothendieck defines the Hodge–Tate group, presumably aiming to compare it with the Zariski closure of the Galois image (Mumford–Tate-type conjecture for p-adic Galois representations).
missed.quote: Regardons le plus petit groupe alg. d'automorphismes G de M⊗Q_ℓ tel que G_C contienne les opérations (λ 0; 0 ξ)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This anticipates Sen (1973) and Serre (1979) if written around 1966–70. The thread breaks off before any statement.

deep.surprise_reason: The page sketches two ideas later developed by others: the Hodge–Tate group (Serre 1979, Sen 1973) and the question of whether p-divisible groups over O_C are determined by lattice plus Hodge–Tate data (Scholze–Weinstein 2013). Both are given only as a definition and a '???', with no results. The dating is uncertain (the notes may be from the 1970s), and Serre was likely discussing similar ideas with Grothendieck at the time. So this is an interesting precursor but not a finished result.
transcription_corrections: 'M⊗Q_ℓ' is as written, but mathematically Q_p is meant.
'[...] de groupes p-divisibles sur K' appears to read '[lié à groupes p-divisibles sur K]'.
C[1] / C[-1] in the formulas denote the Tate twists C(1) / C(-1). The margin writes Ṽ^1 = (V⊗C(1))^π.
